D25·9fw7 — 2026-09-17
chose: The conformance harness is made portable and the goldens re-recorded once for it (D11: at rust-core 6af34c4, reason in golden/MANIFEST.md, previous set kept as golden-4077c9a-symlinked-tmp/): `scratch()` returns the PHYSICAL tmpdir (realpathSync) so `<ROOT>` is the path the child's process.cwd() reports on every platform, and every byte count in a record-delta header is computed over the masked text. The first Linux CI run (draft PR #2) exposed that macOS's /var → /private/var symlink had put every `<ROOT>`-substituted hook path outside the child's physical root, so the goldens held the absolute-path branch of relative(root, path) — a branch Linux never takes — and counts that embedded the recording machine's tmpdir length; 16 goldens changed in exactly those bytes and nothing else. Alongside: the concurrent-append case gets a 120 s timeout (a hosted runner needs tens of seconds for 100 node spawns, and a mid-run timeout leaves children whose cwd the cleanup deletes — the uv_cwd ENOENT in the log), and lock.rs treats Windows' delete-pending PermissionDenied on create_new as contention (retry to the deadline) under cfg(windows) only, which is what made the Windows lock test see overlapping sections.
over: Masking or dropping the byte counts (a wrong count would no longer fail); recording Linux-specific goldens; passing --root explicitly to every step (hides the cwd path the shims really use); treating PermissionDenied as contention on Unix too (a 2 s stall on an unwritable index dir where today the hook runs unlocked at once).
because: Every golden must mean the same bytes on every machine the suite runs on (D1, D11) and CI is now one of those machines; the relative-path branch is the one users hit, so the old goldens were proving the wrong branch; counting over masked text keeps the count a real assertion while removing the only machine-specific input. Both fixes are harness- or platform-only: no hot-path byte moved (27/27 on the reference under both tmpdir layouts and 27/27 through the core).
